info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package git is Git hosting for your org: create repos, clone, push, and see what they cost.

get.summary: Answers the estate's open source figures over a window as series, one per group and metric: by entity, org or ecosystem, per day or per month.
get.description:
Answers the estate's open source figures over a window as series,
one per group and metric: by entity, org or ecosystem, per day or per month.
A running total (stars) takes each entity's last day in a month, a daily count
(downloads) sums its days, and a group sums its entities. A window or a match
too wide to answer whole is refused, never cut. SuperAdmin only.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: Ecosystem keeps one ecosystem's figures; empty keeps every one.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org keeps one GitHub org's figures; empty keeps every org's.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name keeps one entity's figures; empty keeps every entity's.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Metric keeps one metric; empty keeps every metric.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: From is the window's first day, YYYY-MM-DD. Empty means 90 days before to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: To is the window's last day, YYYY-MM-DD. Empty means today (UTC).

parameters.name: granularity
parameters.description: Granularity is "day" (the default, up to 400 days) or "month" (up to 3660).

parameters.name: by
parameters.description:
By groups the series: "name" (the default, one per entity), "org" or
"ecosystem".

post.summary: Writes one batch of the estate's open source figures and package registrations, whole or not at all.
post.description:
Writes one batch of the estate's open source figures and package
registrations, whole or not at all. A figure already held for the same date,
ecosystem, name and metric is replaced, so re-sending a window is safe.
SuperAdmin only.

get.summary: Returns the repositories on the forge (git.hanzo.ai) the caller can read, in every forge namespace their org owns or in the one named, most recently updated first.
get.description:
Returns the repositories on the forge (git.hanzo.ai) the caller can
read, in every forge namespace their org owns or in the one named, most
recently updated first.

Each is named owner/name, the coordinate `repos get`, `runs`, `workflows` and
the browse reads take. The read is the caller's own forge login, so a private
repository they are not given on the forge is not listed. The repositories
this app holds are `repos list`.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description:
Owner lists one forge namespace of the caller's org, such as hanzo-inc.
Empty lists every namespace the org owns.

get.summary: Answers the estate's last 365 days: distinct commits, merges, active repositories and contributors, for the whole estate, each group and each org, a commit count per day, the newest public commits, and one page of public repositories.
get.description:
Answers the estate's last 365 days: distinct commits, merges,
active repositories and contributors, for the whole estate, each group and
each org, a commit count per day, the newest public commits, and one page of
public repositories. Public: private repositories are counted and never named.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org lists one org's repositories; empty lists every org's.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Group lists one group's repositories (hanzo, lux, zoo); empty lists every group's.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page is the repository page, from 1. Anything not positive means 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit is the page size. Anything not positive means 50; the cap is 200.

get.summary: Reads the keys the caller may see: their own, or every key of the org for an org admin.
get.description:
Reads the keys the caller may see: their own, or every key of the org
for an org admin. `repo` narrows to one repository's deploy keys.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repo narrows to one repository's deploy keys.

post.summary: Registers an SSH public key: the caller's own, or — with `repo` — a deploy key for one repository.
post.description:
Registers an SSH public key: the caller's own, or — with `repo` — a deploy
key for one repository. Answers 201. A key already registered anywhere is a 409,
and a repository outside the caller's scope is not found. Deploy keys are an
admin's to register; a user key authenticates its owner into this org only.

delete.summary: Removes a key; a push or fetch with it fails from the next connection.
delete.description:
Removes a key; a push or fetch with it fails from the next connection.
Answers 204. The person who registered it or an org admin may remove it; any
other caller, and an id that is not this org's, is not found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the key's identifier, from the :id path segment.

post.summary: Links every repository of the caller's org that holds no history here and names no link to github.com/<owner>/<name>, where GitHub lets the caller read it.
post.description:
Links every repository of the caller's org that holds no history
here and names no link to github.com/<owner>/<name>, where GitHub lets the
caller read it. A repository with no such namesake is listed and left alone,
and one holding history here is listed and never touched. Nothing is fetched:
a linked repository's cache fills on its first read. Org admins only.

unmatched.name: scratch
unmatched.reason: acme/scratch is not readable as you on GitHub: connect your GitHub account, or ask an org admin

get.summary: Returns the capacity this org has declared and how many daemons have entered each pool.
get.description:
Returns the capacity this org has declared and how many daemons have
entered each pool.

post.summary: Records the capacity an org has, and answers with the secret a runner daemon presents to enter it.
post.description:
Records the capacity an org has, and answers with the secret a
runner daemon presents to enter it.

Declaring is the ONLY way capacity comes to exist: a daemon cannot register
against a pool nobody declared, because the secret it would have to present
does not exist until this runs. Re-declaring an existing pool replaces its
labels and mints a fresh secret; runners already inside it keep working.

get.summary: Returns the repos in the caller's scope, most recently updated first.
get.description:
Returns the repos in the caller's scope, most recently updated
first. The scope is the request principal's — the gateway-minted org and its
optional project — never anything off the wire, so a caller only ever sees its
own. Rows carry no branches or HEAD; read one repo for those.

post.summary: Provisions an empty bare repository in the caller's scope and returns it with its clone URLs.
post.description:
Provisions an empty bare repository in the caller's scope and
returns it with its clone URLs. Answers 201. The name must be unique within
the scope — a repeat is a 409, never a silent overwrite of an existing repo.
The org comes from the validated principal, so a repo is always born owned by
the caller's own tenant.

delete.summary: Removes a repo's metadata and purges its storage.
delete.description:
Removes a repo's metadata and purges its storage. Answers 204 with
no body. The metadata row is the source of truth for existence, so a storage
purge that fails is logged and the delete still succeeds — and a second call
is a 404, not a second delete. A repository this app does not hold is looked
for where getRepo looks next, the org's made workspace on the forge, so a
customer's own repository (or the copy a GitHub link made there) is one a
delete can reach, as their list already shows it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

get.summary: Returns one repo with its live ref state: every branch name and the resolved HEAD commit.
get.description:
Returns one repo with its live ref state: every branch name and the
resolved HEAD commit. Both are read from the object store on each call, so an
empty repo reports no branches and an empty head rather than failing. A repo
outside the caller's scope is not found.

A name with an owner, hanzo-inc/cloud, is the repository on the forge
(git.hanzo.ai), its one home, read there as the caller in a forge namespace
their org owns; the tree and blob reads take the same coordinate.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

patch.summary: Flips a repo's public bit, the one mutable repo setting today.
patch.description:
Flips a repo's public bit, the one mutable repo setting today.
Public grants ANONYMOUS fetch only; push and the whole control plane stay
org-authed. Returns the updated repo.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo to update, from the :name path segment.

get.summary: Returns one file's bytes at one revision.
get.description:
Returns one file's bytes at one revision. Text comes back verbatim,
binary comes back base64, and a file past the 1 MiB view cap comes back marked
truncated with NO content — the client is expected to clone instead. A
repository in the organization's own code workspace on the forge is read from
there.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo to read, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is a branch, tag or commit; empty means the repo's HEAD.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path is repo-relative; empty is the tree root. Traversal is stripped.

get.summary: Walks a ref's history newest first, or one path's history when a path is given.
get.description:
Walks a ref's history newest first, or one path's history when a
path is given. There is no cursor: the page is the newest `limit` commits.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo to read, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is the branch, tag or commit to walk back from; empty means HEAD.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path narrows the history to commits touching it; empty walks the whole ref.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the page. Anything not positive means 50; the cap is 100.

get.summary: Reads what a commit's contexts say, and the one word they say together.
get.description:
Reads what a commit's contexts say, and the one word they say
together.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repository, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: sha
parameters.description: SHA is the full commit hash, from the :sha path segment.

post.summary: States a commit's status.
post.description:
States a commit's status. Answers 201. Stating a context that already
spoke replaces its word. A repository outside the caller's scope is not found.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repository, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: sha
parameters.description: SHA is the full commit hash the status is about, from the :sha path segment.

get.summary: Returns every file a glob selects at one revision, WITH its bytes and the revision they came from.
get.description:
Returns every file a glob selects at one revision, WITH its bytes
and the revision they came from. It is the read a delivery generator makes:
one call answers "what is the inventory at this commit, and what does it say",
where listing and then fetching would be a request per file.

Returning the resolved revision matters as much as the bytes. A generator that
lists at `main` and then reads at `main` can straddle a push and assemble half
its inventory from one commit and half from the next; resolving once makes the
whole read consistent by construction.

A file past the read cap comes back Truncated with no content rather than
being dropped. A caller building a desired set has to know the difference
between "this file is empty" and "this file was not read" — silently omitting
it is how a pruning reconcile deletes what the missing file declared.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo to read, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is a branch, tag or commit; empty means the repo's HEAD.

parameters.name: glob
parameters.description:
Glob selects files, matched segment by segment so `*` never crosses a `/`.
`**` matches zero or more whole segments.

post.summary: Repacks a repo into one bitmapped pack and rewrites its commit-graph, so the next clone reuses the bitmap instead of walking the whole object graph.
post.description:
Repacks a repo into one bitmapped pack and rewrites its commit-graph, so
the next clone reuses the bitmap instead of walking the whole object graph.
Idempotent, and safe to interrupt — git swaps both artifacts atomically. It
runs under one pack slot with the same memory bounds as a clone, so it can
block behind heavy pack traffic rather than compete with it. Storage usage is
re-measured afterwards, since a repack reclaims space.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

post.summary: Moves a repository whose history is HERE to the forge (git.hanzo.ai), the one home of a repository no other host holds, and links it there: the repository is made in the org's own namespace on the forge, every branch and tag is pushed to it, the forge's refs are read back and must equal these, and only then does the row name the forge as its link, so this copy becomes the cache it can be fetched back into.
post.description:
Moves a repository whose history is HERE to the forge (git.hanzo.ai),
the one home of a repository no other host holds, and links it there: the
repository is made in the org's own namespace on the forge, every branch and
tag is pushed to it, the forge's refs are read back and must equal these, and
only then does the row name the forge as its link, so this copy becomes the
cache it can be fetched back into. A forge repository of that name that
already exists is refused, never overwritten. Org admins only.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repository, from the :name path segment.

post.summary: Records that a repository's history lives on another host, making the repository first when the org has none of that name.
post.description:
Records that a repository's history lives on another host, making
the repository first when the org has none of that name. Nothing is copied:
a read is served from a cache filled from the host, as the host lets the
caller read, and a push goes to the host. A repository whose history is HERE
is refused (409): a link would hide what only this store holds.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repository, from the :name path segment. It is made when the
org has none of that name.

get.summary: Returns a repo's pull requests, newest number first — what is waiting to be reviewed, and what has already landed.
get.description:
Returns a repo's pull requests, newest number first — what is
waiting to be reviewed, and what has already landed. Narrow it with
?state=open or ?state=merged; omit state for every proposal.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: State narrows the list to "open" or "merged". Omit it for every proposal.

post.summary: Proposes a branch for merging and returns it with its number.
post.description:
Proposes a branch for merging and returns it with its number. Answers
201. Both branches must already exist — a proposal naming a branch nobody
pushed is a typo, not a plan — and base defaults to the repo's default branch.

Proposing the same head into the same base twice is a 409 while the first
proposal is still open, so a retried agent run leaves ONE thing to review
rather than a pile of identical ones. A repo outside the caller's scope is a
404, exactly as reading it is.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo the proposal belongs to, from the :name path segment.

get.summary: Returns one pull request by its per-repo number.
get.description:
Returns one pull request by its per-repo number. A number belonging to
another tenant's repo is not found, exactly as the repo itself is not.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Number is the proposal's per-repo number, from the :number path segment.

post.summary: Merges an open pull request by FAST-FORWARDING base to head, and answers the proposal in its merged state with the revision base now points at.
post.description:
Merges an open pull request by FAST-FORWARDING base to head, and
answers the proposal in its merged state with the revision base now points at.

It merges only when base is already an ancestor of head — the case where head
contains every commit base has, so moving the branch loses nothing and invents
nothing. When base has moved on independently, this REFUSES with 409 and says
so: a real three-way merge is not implemented here, and reporting one would
claim a result these bytes do not produce. Rebase head onto base and merge
again.

The move is judged by the same ref policy a `git push` of it would face, and
fires the same build and notify reactions, so merging is not a way around
either. Merging an already-merged proposal is a 409.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Number is the proposal's per-repo number, from the :number path segment.

post.summary: Lands a set of files as one commit without a git client — the hanzo.app builder's push.
post.description:
Lands a set of files as one commit without a git client — the
hanzo.app builder's push. The repo is CREATED on first push, the files are
merged onto the branch tip (unlisted files survive), and the same
push-to-deploy hook a real receive-pack fires is fired, so downstream this is
indistinguishable from a `git push`.

It is for generated content. Changing CI through it needs an org admin (403
otherwise), and a workflow whose newest change came in through it is not run
automatically; CI written through git runs as usual.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo to push into, from the :name path segment. It is CREATED
on first push if it does not exist.

get.summary: Returns the README at the tree root as plain text — unrendered, so the caller decides how to present it.
get.description:
Returns the README at the tree root as plain text — unrendered, so
the caller decides how to present it. A repo with no README is not found.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo to read, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is a branch, tag or commit; empty means the repo's HEAD.

get.summary: Lists a repo's branches, tags and default branch — what a branch picker needs in one call.
get.description:
Lists a repo's branches, tags and default branch — what a branch
picker needs in one call. Unlike the other read ops it tolerates a repo with no
commits: the ref sets come back empty and the default branch is still named.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

get.summary: Returns a repo's Slack subscriptions — which channels the lifecycle notifier posts this repo's push and deploy events to.
get.description:
Returns a repo's Slack subscriptions — which channels the
lifecycle notifier posts this repo's push and deploy events to.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

post.summary: Binds a Slack channel to a repo, so the lifecycle notifier posts that repo's push and deploy events there.
post.description:
Binds a Slack channel to a repo, so the lifecycle notifier posts
that repo's push and deploy events there. Answers 201. The same channel twice
on one repo is a 409; a repo outside the caller's scope is a 404, exactly as
reading it is.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo to subscribe, from the :name path segment.

delete.summary: Removes one Slack subscription from a repo; the notifier stops posting that repo's events to that channel.
delete.description:
Removes one Slack subscription from a repo; the notifier stops
posting that repo's events to that channel. Answers 204 with no body. An id
that is not this repo's subscription is not found.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the row to remove, from the :id path segment.

get.summary: Returns a repo's outbound mirror targets — the downstream remotes the mirror reactor pushes to whenever a push lands here.
get.description:
Returns a repo's outbound mirror targets — the downstream remotes
the mirror reactor pushes to whenever a push lands here.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

post.summary: Registers a downstream remote the repo's advanced refs are pushed to whenever a push lands here.
post.description:
Registers a downstream remote the repo's advanced refs are pushed to
whenever a push lands here. Answers 201. The URL must be https to a host on the
mirror allowlist (github.com / gitlab.com): the same set the mirror credential
may be sent to, so a target can never capture the shared token or point the push
at an internal service. Any embedded userinfo is stripped — credentials ride
env-only at push time and never enter the stored URL. One mirror per host per
repo; a second is a 409.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo whose advanced refs are pushed downstream, from the :name
path segment.

delete.summary: Removes one outbound mirror target; later pushes stop being forwarded to it.
delete.description:
Removes one outbound mirror target; later pushes stop being
forwarded to it. Answers 204 with no body. Nothing is done to the downstream
remote itself — only this repo's intent to push there is dropped.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the row to remove, from the :id path segment.

get.summary: Lists the immediate children of one directory at one revision, directories before files.
get.description:
Lists the immediate children of one directory at one revision,
directories before files. It does not recurse — walk down a level at a time.
A repository in the organization's own code workspace on the forge is listed
from there.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo to read, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is a branch, tag or commit; empty means the repo's HEAD.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path is repo-relative; empty is the tree root. Traversal is stripped.

get.summary: Returns the runners that can run the caller's work, each with when it was last heard from, and the health of every pool.
get.description:
Returns the runners that can run the caller's work, each with
when it was last heard from, and the health of every pool.

First the forge's: the runners registered on git.hanzo.ai, which run every
repository whose home is there — the platform starts one for each job the
forge queues, labelled as the job asked. Then the daemons registered into this
org's own declared pools. Pools groups the forge's by label set, with the
caller's jobs queued on each, so a label set with work waiting and no runner
online — a dead pool — is visible.

The forge's runners serve every tenant and are named for the repository whose
job they took, so they are listed by name to a SuperAdmin; anyone else sees
the pools their own queued jobs wait on — the jobs of repositories the forge
lets them read — with how many runners carry each and when one was last heard.

get.summary: Returns this org's runs, newest first.
get.description:
Returns this org's runs, newest first.

A repository named owner/name is on the forge, and its runs are the forge's:
the newest, or, when a ref is named, every run on the commit it resolves to,
each with its jobs and steps and the ref's verdict in State.

parameters.name: repo
ref
parameters.description:
Ref keeps one branch, tag or commit. On the forge it is resolved to its
commit and every run on that commit is answered with its jobs, and State
says whether the ref is green; here it keeps the runs of that branch.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the answer; 0 means the default of 50, and 200 is the ceiling.

post.summary: Runs a repository's workflows at a ref, on demand.
post.description:
Runs a repository's workflows at a ref, on demand.

It takes the SAME path a push takes: the request is recorded in the journal
and delivered from there, so an explicit run and a pushed one are one
mechanism with one idempotency rule and not two that can disagree. Asking
twice for the same commit yields the same run.

get.summary: Returns one run with its jobs and their steps.
get.description:
Returns one run with its jobs and their steps.

A run of a forge repository is addressed by its id on the forge and the
repository, owner/name; one this app scheduled by its id alone.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the run to read, from the :id path segment.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description:
Repo is the forge repository the run belongs to, owner/name; empty for a
run this app scheduled.

get.summary: Returns what a run's jobs wrote: one job's log, named by its id or its name, or by default the log of every job that failed, with the lines in each that say what failed picked out.
get.description:
Returns what a run's jobs wrote: one job's log, named by its id
or its name, or by default the log of every job that failed, with the lines
in each that say what failed picked out.

A run of a forge repository is addressed by its id on the forge and the
repository, owner/name; one this app scheduled by its id alone.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID is the run, from the :id path segment: its id on the forge for a forge
repository, or the id this app gave it.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description:
Repo is the forge repository the run belongs to, owner/name; empty for a
run this app scheduled.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description:
Job is one job of the run, by its id or its name. Empty reads every job
that failed.

get.summary: Returns per-repo and total storage bytes for the caller's org — the queryable, per-tenant number commerce and o11y meter on.
get.description:
Returns per-repo and total storage bytes for the caller's org — the
queryable, per-tenant number commerce and o11y meter on. It spans EVERY
project sub-scope, unlike the repo list, so a billing consumer sees the whole
tenant footprint in one call. Sizes are last-measured values (create, push,
mirror and gc each re-measure), not a live walk of the disk.

post.summary: Retired — push-to-deploy has no inbound webhook
post.description:
GONE (410). Push-to-deploy is not triggered by an inbound webhook. A push into this host's own git server fires the builder in-process, and a repository whose canonical home is GitHub is delivered by the Hanzo Platform GitHub App to POST /v1/provider/github/webhook. The forge does not report a push over HTTP.

Every delivery answers 410 whatever it carries — this endpoint reads no body and authenticates nothing.

410 rather than 404, because the address was real and its meaning moved, which is the distinction 410 carries. A 404 from this estate is ambiguous: Hanzo Git serves /v1, so /api/v1 404s too and reads as "the API is switched off". A retired endpoint says it is retired and names its replacement, so the answer carries its own fix.

get.summary: Reports the workflows a repository declares at a ref and which declared pool would execute each job — the answer to "would a push here run, and where".
get.description:
Reports the workflows a repository declares at a ref and which
declared pool would execute each job — the answer to "would a push here run,
and where".

A repository named owner/name is read from the forge, at the commit the ref
resolves to, in the same two directories the forge reads (.hanzo/workflows,
then .github/workflows).

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description:
Repo is the repository whose workflows to read: owner/name on the forge,
such as hanzo-inc/cloud, or a bare name this app holds.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is the branch to read them at; empty means the default.

post.summary: Sets the org's code workspace up for the caller and answers it: the namespace, made when the org has none, and the caller's forge account and seat there.
post.description:
Sets the org's code workspace up for the caller and answers it:
the namespace, made when the org has none, and the caller's forge account and
seat there. Idempotent. The estate's namespace is answered from the closed
table and nobody is enrolled in it. A seat is a person's: an API key or an
application is refused, and a SuperAdmin acting in another org reads the
workspace as it is and makes nothing.

post.summary: Accept a push, and turn it into a build
post.description:
The pack-transfer phase of a push, and the point at which a push becomes an EVENT. NEVER ANONYMOUS: a push always requires an authenticated org, and the org in the path must equal it.

Once the pack is on disk the repository's storage usage is metered and a build is fired for every branch whose tip actually moved, computed from the before/after branch diff rather than from what the client claimed. That runs on a cancel-immune context, so a client that hangs up the moment its push lands still gets its build, and it runs even when git itself exited non-zero — the refs on disk are the ground truth. Repacking housekeeping is detached and never blocks the response.

A Content-Type other than `application/x-git-receive-pack-request` is 400. Addressed under the API prefix, with the PROJECT as a middle path segment: project scope otherwise rides a header a git client cannot send, so this path is the only usable remote for a project-scoped repository. This is git's own wire protocol, not an API call to make by hand: point a git client at the clone URL and it makes this request itself.

post.summary: Serve a clone or fetch
post.description:
The pack-transfer phase of a clone or fetch: the request and the response are git's binary pack protocol, streamed straight through git itself — request body to git's stdin, git's stdout to the response — so a multi-gigabyte clone never lands in this process's memory.

A PUBLIC repository is fetched anonymously; a private one requires its own org, and a wrong or absent org is 404 rather than a hint that the repository exists. A Content-Type other than `application/x-git-upload-pack-request` is 400. Addressed under the API prefix, with the PROJECT as a middle path segment: project scope otherwise rides a header a git client cannot send, so this path is the only usable remote for a project-scoped repository. This is git's own wire protocol, not an API call to make by hand: point a git client at the clone URL and it makes this request itself.

get.summary: Advertise a repository's refs to a git client
get.description:
The ref-advertisement phase of git's smart-HTTP protocol — the first request a clone, a fetch and a push all make. `?service=` selects which: `git-upload-pack` advertises for a fetch, `git-receive-pack` for a push, and any other value is 400.

ANONYMOUS ONLY FOR FETCH, AND ONLY ON A PUBLIC REPOSITORY. The push advertisement always requires an authenticated org, and where a path org is present it must equal the authenticated one. A private repository reached without its org is 404, indistinguishable from one that does not exist. Addressed under the API prefix, with the PROJECT as a middle path segment: project scope otherwise rides a header a git client cannot send, so this path is the only usable remote for a project-scoped repository. This is git's own wire protocol, not an API call to make by hand: point a git client at the clone URL and it makes this request itself.

post.summary: Accept a push, and turn it into a build
post.description:
The pack-transfer phase of a push, and the point at which a push becomes an EVENT. NEVER ANONYMOUS: a push always requires an authenticated org, and the org in the path must equal it.

Once the pack is on disk the repository's storage usage is metered and a build is fired for every branch whose tip actually moved, computed from the before/after branch diff rather than from what the client claimed. That runs on a cancel-immune context, so a client that hangs up the moment its push lands still gets its build, and it runs even when git itself exited non-zero — the refs on disk are the ground truth. Repacking housekeeping is detached and never blocks the response.

A Content-Type other than `application/x-git-receive-pack-request` is 400. Addressed under the API prefix, so `git clone https://<host>/v1/git/<org>/<repo>.git` works on any host the binary serves. This is git's own wire protocol, not an API call to make by hand: point a git client at the clone URL and it makes this request itself.

Truncated marks a file past the 1 MiB view cap. No content is sent —

State is the worst of the contexts: failure, error, warning, pending, else
success. A commit with no status is pending.

project.description:
Project narrows the repo to a sub-scope of the org. Omit it to use the
caller's own X-Project-Id scope; it can never widen past the caller's org.

returned.

rev.description: Rev is the full revision the ref resolved to — pin follow-up reads to it.

maintained.description: Maintained is always true; the call fails rather than reporting false.

repacking drops the packs it supersedes.

by.description: By is what the series are grouped by.

from.description: From is the window's first day.

granularity.description: Granularity is the points' granularity, "day" or "month".

to.description: To is the window's last day.

cut.description:
Cut says the log is longer than 32 MiB and was read no further, so Log
ends where the read stopped rather than where the job's output did.

failing.description:
Failing are the lines of the whole log that say what failed, in order: a
failing test and what it reported, a failing package, a panic, a compiler
or vet diagnostic, and an error the runner annotated. At most 100.

fault.description: Fault is why this job's log could not be read; the other jobs still answer.

log.description: Log is the end of the job's output, at most 256 KiB, in whole lines.

name.description: Name is the job's name in the workflow document.

status.description: Status is waiting, running, or how the job ended.

truncated.description: Truncated says Log is the end of a longer log.

name.description: Name is the job's id in the workflow document.

needs.description: Needs are the jobs this one waits for.

pool.description:
Pool is where the job would run. Here it is the declared pool carrying
every one of those labels, or empty when no pool does — which is the answer
to "why is nothing running". On the forge it is the label set, sorted and
joined by "+", that the platform starts a runner for when the job queues,
and empty when no node in the cluster can run it (macOS, Windows) or the job
asks for nothing.

runsOn.description: RunsOn is the labels the job asked for.

uses.description:
Uses is the reusable workflow the job calls instead of running steps of its
own, such as hanzoai/ci/.github/workflows/build.yml@v2.1.21; its jobs run
where that workflow says.

key.description: Key is the public key as one authorized_keys line ("ssh-ed25519 AAAA… comment"). Required.

readOnly.description: ReadOnly limits a deploy key to fetching. Ignored for a user key.

creator.description: Creator is the subject that registered it.

fingerprint.description: Fingerprint is the key's SHA256 fingerprint, the form `ssh-keygen -l` prints.

id.description: ID is the key's identifier ("key_…"), the handle to delete it by.

kind.description: Kind is "user" for a person's key or "deploy" for a repository's.

readOnly.description: ReadOnly is whether a deploy key may only fetch.

repo.description: Repo is the repository a deploy key is bound to; empty for a user key.

title.description: Title is the label given at registration.

cloneUrl.description: CloneURL is the address its history is fetched from and pushed to.

name.description: Name is the repository's name on its provider.

owner.description: Owner is the account the repository belongs to on its provider.

provider.description:
Provider is "github", "forge" (git.hanzo.ai, Hanzo's own), or "git" for
any other host.

owner.description:
Owner is the GitHub account a repository named n is looked for under, as
github.com/<owner>/<n>. Empty is the account the estate's table names for
the org; an org it does not name must give one.

name.description:
Name is the repository, from the :name path segment. It is made when the
org has none of that name.

project.description: Project is the sub-scope to make it in; empty uses the caller's own.

source.description:
Source is where its history lives: an http(s) clone address, such as
https://github.com/acme/widgets.git. Its host must let the caller read it.

held.description:
Held are the repositories that hold their own history here, which a link
would hide.

linked.description: Linked are the repositories it linked, each to its namesake on GitHub.

unmatched.description:
Unmatched are the repositories it left as they were, each with what GitHub
answered: no namesake readable as the caller is never replaced by a guess.

date.description: Date is YYYY-MM-DD at day granularity and YYYY-MM at month granularity.

or "dockerhub".

metric.description:
Metric is one of stars, forks, open_issues, watchers, downloads_total and
pulls_total (running totals), or downloads, pulls, release_downloads,
clones, views, unique_clones and unique_views (that day's count).

name.description: Name is the entity: owner/repo on GitHub, the package's name on a registry.

org.description: Org is the GitHub org the entity belongs to, the per-org breakdown's key.

value.description: Value is the figure. Never negative.

key.description:
Key names the group: an ecosystem ("npm"), an org ("hanzoai"), or an
entity as ecosystem/name ("npm/@hanzo/ui", "github/hanzoai/ui").

kind.description:
Kind is how the metric rolls up: "gauge" takes an entity's last day in a
month, "count" sums its days. A group sums its entities either way.

metric.description: Metric is the metric's name, as posted ("stars", "downloads").

points.description:
Points are the series' values, oldest first. A day or month with no figure
has no point.

data.description: Data holds the repo's outbound mirror targets.

Host is an optional assertion of the target's hostname. The authoritative
host is the one in URL; a value that disagrees with it is refused.

url.description: URL is the canonical https remote, with any embedded credentials stripped.

Base is the branch the work is proposed INTO, by short name. Defaults to
the repo's default branch, which is where a proposal goes when nobody says
otherwise.

body.description: Body is the longer description. Optional.

head.description:
Head is the branch holding the work, by short name (agent/fix-503).
Required, and must already exist.

name.description: Name is the package's name on its registry.

upstream.description:

of its address; it is stored as github.com/<owner>/<repo>.

public.description:
Public flips anonymous read access. Omit it and the request is refused —
there is nothing else to update yet.

HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE — only a digest is stored — so a lost one is
replaced by declaring the pool again.

busy.description: Busy is how many of those are executing a job now.

labels.description: Labels are the labels in it.

none ever was, or the forge does not say.

label set. Queued with nothing Online is a dead pool.

runners.description: Runners is how many registered forge runners carry every one of them.

labels.description: Labels are what a workflow's `runs-on:` selects this pool by.

name.description: Name is the pool's handle in this org.

runners.description:

capacity is declared and nothing has turned up to provide it.

data.description: Data holds the repo's pull requests, newest number first.

author.description: Author is the user who opened it; empty for a caller with no user.

body.description: Body is the longer description; empty when none was given.

head.description: Head is the branch holding the work.

content.description: Content is the file's bytes, carried per Encoding.

branch.description:
Branch to advance; empty means "main". A fresh branch that is the repo's
first also becomes HEAD.

message.description: Message is the commit message; empty gets a generated one.

name.description:

rows.description:

written.description: Written is the number of figures written.

content.description: Content is the file's text, verbatim and unrendered.

path.description: Path is the file the README was found at (README.md, README, …).

name.description: Name is the short ref name ("main", "v1.2.0"), not the full refs/… path.

sha.description: SHA is the full commit hash the ref resolves to.

branches.description: Branches are the repo's heads; empty on a repo with no commits.

default.description: Default is the branch name a caller gets when it asks for no ref.

tags.description: Tags are the repo's tags; empty when there are none.

data.description: Data holds the repos in scope, most recently updated first.

branches.description:

defaultBranch.description: DefaultBranch is where HEAD points on a fresh repo ("main").

link.description:

name.description: Name is the org-unique handle, and the last path segment of both URLs below.

estate's collector registered them (POST /v1/admin/git/metrics).

project.description:

default scope.

public.description:
Public grants ANONYMOUS read (fetch) only; push and the whole control plane

fault.description:
Fault says why the forge's runners are missing from this answer, when the
forge could not be read; the daemons here are listed either way.

pools.description:
Pools is each label set a forge runner answers to or a queued job asks for,
with how many runners carry it, how many of those are online, and how many
of the caller's jobs wait on it. A pool with jobs queued and no runner
online is a dead pool.

busy.description: Busy is whether it is executing a job now. Known for a forge runner only.

ephemeral.description:
Ephemeral means the daemon takes ONE job and exits, so it is not expected
back and its absence is not a fault.

forge.description:
Forge is true for a runner registered on the forge (git.hanzo.ai), which
runs the repositories whose home is there, and false for a daemon in one of
this org's declared pools.

labels.description: Labels are what the daemon last said it can do.

lastActive.description:
LastActive is when it was last EXECUTING a job, in unix seconds. It lags
LastOnline on an idle daemon, which is how the two differ.

lastOnline.description: LastOnline is when it last called at all, in unix seconds.

name.description: Name is what the daemon called itself when it registered.

online.description:
Online is whether it was heard from lately: within the forge's offline
window for a forge runner, within a minute for a daemon here.

pool.description:
Pool is the declared capacity it entered; for a runner on the forge, the
label set it answers to, sorted and joined by "+".

version.description: Version is the runner build the daemon last reported.

context.description:
Context names what is speaking ("ci/lint"). Stating the same context again
replaces its earlier word. Defaults to "default".

description.description: Description is a short human sentence about the state.

name.description: Name is the repository, from the :name path segment.

sha.description: SHA is the full commit hash the status is about, from the :sha path segment.

state.description: State is pending, success, failure, error, warning or skipped. Required.

targetUrl.description: TargetURL is where a person reads more: a run page, a build log.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the context first spoke, RFC 3339 UTC.

creator.description: Creator is who stated it: the principal's subject, or "run" for the engine.

description.description: Description is the short sentence the context gave.

id.description: ID is the status row's identifier.

state.description: State is pending, success, failure, error, warning or skipped.

targetUrl.description: TargetURL is where a person reads more; empty when none was given.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is when it last spoke, RFC 3339 UTC.

channel.description:
Channel is the Slack channel the notifier posts to — an id (C…/G…), a
#name, or a bare name. Required.

events.description:
Events narrows delivery to these lifecycle kinds (push.landed,
deploy.live, deploy.failed). Omit it to receive every deliverable kind; a
kind that is never posted to Slack is refused rather than silently dropped.

name.description: Name is the repo to subscribe, from the :name path segment.

channel.description: Channel is the Slack channel id or name the notifier posts to.

events.description: Events is the kind filter; absent means every deliverable kind.

id.description: ID is the subscription's identifier ("sub_…"), the handle to delete it by.

repo.description: Repo is the repo whose lifecycle events are delivered.

mode.description: Mode is the octal git file mode ("100644", "040000", "120000").

name.description: Name is the entry's own name, no directory part.

path.description: Path is the entry's full repo-relative path.

size.description: Size is the file's byte length; 0 for a directory.

type.description: Type is "tree" for a directory, "blob" for a file.

entries.description: Entries are the immediate children, directories before files.

name.description: Name is the repository.

reason.description: Reason is what GitHub answered about its namesake.

name.description: Name is the repo's org-unique handle.

project.description: Project is the sub-scope the repo lives in; absent for the default scope.

sizeBytes.description: SizeBytes is the repo's on-disk size at its last measurement.

repos.description: Repos is every repo the org owns, across every project sub-scope.

totalBytes.description: TotalBytes is the sum over Repos — the org's whole git footprint.

commit.description: Commit is the commit the ref resolved to, which the documents were read at.

data.description: Data is the workflows the repository declares at the ref.

attempt.description: Attempt counts the forge's re-runs of this run, from 1.

commit.description: Commit is the commit being run, in full.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the run was opened, in unix seconds.

endedAt.description: EndedAt is when it finished, RFC 3339; absent until it has.

event.description: Event is what caused the run, e.g. "push".

jobs.description:
Jobs are the run's jobs in the order they were created, with their steps:
answered by `runs get`, and by `runs list` when a ref names one commit.

number.description:
Number is the run's position in its repository, counting from 1 — the
handle a person uses ("#4").

ref.description: Ref is the full ref, e.g. "refs/heads/main".

repo.description: Repo is the repository the run is for.

startedAt.description: StartedAt is when it started executing, RFC 3339; absent until it has.

status.description:
Status is waiting, running, success, failure, cancelled or skipped: waiting
until a runner takes it (or, on the forge, while a job it needs is still
going), running while it executes, and then how it ended.

title.description: Title is the run's display title on the forge, usually its commit's subject.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is when its status last changed, in unix seconds.

url.description: URL is the run's page on the forge.

workflow.description:
Workflow is the path of the document being run, e.g.
".hanzo/workflows/ci.yml".

commit.description:
Commit is the commit a ref named, when the listing asked for one: the runs
are the ones on it, and a branch that moves does not move them.

data.description: Data is the runs in scope, newest first.

state.description:
State answers "is this ref green?" when the listing named a forge ref:
passed, failed, running, queued or none. It is read over the latest attempt
of each workflow on the commit: any failed or cancelled run or job is
failed; otherwise any still going is running, any waiting for a runner is
queued, and when everything finished as success or skipped it is passed.
none means nothing ran.

fault.description: Fault is why this document cannot run at all, when it cannot be read.

jobs.description: Jobs is what it declares, and where each would run.

name.description: Name is the document's path in the repository.

login.description: Login is the caller's forge account in a made workspace.

made.description: Made says the platform made it for the org; false is the estate's.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
